newsitem.title: UK: BT says has no plans for Concert rights issue.
newsitem.headline: BT says has no plans for Concert rights issue.

text.p: British Telecommunications (BT) Plc said on Sunday it had no plans to launch a rights issue to help fund its giant merger, valued at around $20 billion, with U.S. international carrier MCI Communications Corp.

BT, which has a gearing level of less than five percent, is paying about 4.5 billion pounds for the proposed deal in the form of 2.2 billion pound special dividend for its own investors and 2.3 billion pounds to MCI shareholders.

With a cash mountain of around 2.6 billion pounds, the company would be looking at "a variety of options" to fund the outstanding debt, which will help raise its gearing level to about 65 percent along with other planned investments.
But John Brougham, director of investor relations at BT, told Reuters, "BT has no plans for a rights issue."

The deal to create a new company called Concert Plc, the world's second largest international carrier behind U.S. telecoms giant AT&T Corp, values MCI at about $17.2 billion and BT at 22.6 billion pounds, according to share prices at the close of business last Thursday.

Under the terms, for every MCI share, investors will get 0.45 new Concert American Depositary Shares (ADSs) -- the same as 0.54 BT ADSs which represents 10 ordinary shares in BT -- and a cash payment of $6.0.
Based on the fully diluted number of MCI shares, the cash payment to MCI investors will total up to 2.3 billion stg.

BT already owns 20 percent of MCI and hopes that a full- scale merger will help place it in a better position to compete for the domestic and international markets in the U.S. -- the world's biggest market -- and forge new links in the Asia Pacific region -- the fastest growing market in the world.
